subject: One-time infrastructure subsidy request — BerkeleyTech enterprise pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Claire Nolan <claire@berkeleytech.com>, Austin Reed <a.reed@berkeleytech.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot request: one-time infra subsidy for enterprise POC

Evelyn / Kim — looping you in on a time-sensitive ask from BerkeleyTech. Short summary:

- Opportunity: 3-month enterprise pilot (production inference on dedicated infra) targeting 50M tokens/month; if successful, customer will commit to a multi-region Dedicated contract in Q4.
- Ask: BerkeleyTech needs a one-time infrastructure subsidy to offset initial heavy KV cache/throughput costs — they are asking for a $30k credit applied over the first 90 days (applies to infra portion only).
- Why now: They have a competing internal evaluation window and want infra cost isolation to avoid upfront cloud overages during the POC. Without a subsidy they may pause the pilot.

Why I think this is strategic: 1) Large potential ARR (> $600k ARR on 3-yr committed plan if pilot converts), 2) Reference value in higher-ed vertical, 3) They already committed to SSO + SOC2 scoping (so lower security lift).

Requested action: need VP/CFO-level signoff to approve the $30k one-time subsidy (deviates from standard onboarding floors). I attached the draft SOW and the HubSpot deal link — see the financial sketch in the next email from Kim.

Attachments: BerkeleyTech-Pilot-SOW.pdf (SOW, scope, acceptance criteria)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call if you want to walk the numbers.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Mobile: 415-555-0147
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: one-time infra subsidy for enterprise POC

Karthik — thanks for the summary. A couple quick clarifying questions before I sign off:

- Confirm the conversion trigger: what minimum volume / MRR in month 6 do we need to see to consider this a successful pilot? Put a numeric threshold in the SOW.
- Is the $30k underwriting the infra only or are we offsetting per-token charges as well? Need a clean separation in the billing.
- Precedent risk: have we done similar subsidies for other higher-ed pilots in the last 12 months? If so, what was the conversion rate?

Kim — can you run a quick margin impact and precedent check and share a recommended approval envelope? I prefer a tight, conditional approval (if we do this it should be timeboxed and instrumented).

I will hold the signature until I have those items.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart | VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
Note: please add any finance notes to the HubSpot deal thread for auditability.
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: one-time infra subsidy for enterprise POC

Evelyn / Karthik — ran the numbers. Short version: approve with constraints. Details below and attached calc.

Financial summary (BT pilot):
- Subsidy requested: $30,000 applied to infra (GPU hours / fixed capacity) over 90 days.
- Incremental gross margin hit (estimate): ~$18k over the 90-day period (assumes 40% gross margin on infra).
- Upside: modeled conversion probability 35% given current engagement; NPV if converted to expected 3-yr committed number > $420k (post discounts).

Recommended approval envelope:
1) Approve up to $30k one-time infra subsidy, but paid as a conditional credit in two installments (50% at pilot start, 50% on completion after acceptance criteria).
2) Subsidy must be limited to infra line items — no token/per-response credits.
3) Pilot acceptance must include the conversion metric: >= $50k MRR equivalent or signed Letter of Intent within 6 months.
4) Limit to a single precedent: record approval in HubSpot and flag as "one-off subsidy — exec approved" so it requires Director+ signoff to re-run.

Attachments: BT-fin-calc.xlsx (simple P&L and sensitivity).

If you want, I can draft the memo text for your signature, Evelyn.

—Kimberly Park
Kimberly Park | Head of Finance, Commercial | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Nolan <claire@berkeleytech.com>, Austin Reed <a.reed@berkeleytech.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: one-time infra subsidy for enterprise POC

Thanks — Kim, that calc is helpful and reasonable. Approving with conditions below (finalized memo for the record):

Executive approval (Evelyn Hart, VP Commercial Operations):
- Authorization: Approve a one-time infrastructure subsidy of up to $30,000 for the BerkeleyTech 90-day pilot.
- Conditions:
  * Credit is applied to infra-only charges and issued in two installments (50% at pilot start, 50% after acceptance criteria met).
  * Acceptance criteria (to be included in SOW): production inference throughput >= target (as defined in attached SOW) and evidence of integration with their internal systems; conversion metric is >= $50k MRR equivalent within 6 months or a signed LOI.
  * Record and precedent control: label HubSpot deal BT-ENT-2027-05 with tag "one-off-exec-subsidy"; this decision is a single precedent and requires Director+ commercial signoff for any similar future request.

Karthik — please update the SOW to include the numeric acceptance criteria, route the HubSpot deal update, and have the customer initial the subsidy section. Claire / Austin — thank you for the openness here; we look forward to a productive pilot.

I will BCC Finance and Legal and will route a short DocuSign amendment for the subsidy clause.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart | VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
